page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is a virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. However, multi-core performance metrics, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, while small-block cached read bandwidth is relatively weak.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core execution, this instance is suitable for workloads that do not heavily parallelize but require consistent single-threaded performance. It is appropriate for light web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale single-threaded applications. However, it is less optimal for highly parallelized tasks, database operations, or heavy multi-threaded compilation due to its lower multi-core benchmark results.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. With 2 physical cores and hyperthreading enabled, it delivers a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU execution, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests. Conversely, multi-core performance, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Large-block memory bandwidth and single-threaded compression tasks perform at an average level. This resource profile is best suited for general-purpose workloads, light web serving, and single-threaded applications that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation but do not require intensive multi-core scaling or high-speed local storage.
